NO. 023 · Songbirds & City Birds / Laniidae · Shrikes

Long-tailed Shrike

棕背伯劳 · zōng bèi bó láo Lanius schach
Resident Common 24–28 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

An eagle's eye on a sparrow's body — the little butcher

Twenty-odd centimetres long with the heart of a raptor: black mask, hooked bill, hard stare. The Long-tailed Shrike takes insects, lizards, mice and even small birds, and impales what it cannot finish on thorns to dry — its most famous habit.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • HeadCrown grey to black with a broad black band through the eye; that glare is the classic shrike look.
  • PlumageBack and scapulars rufous (varying between subspecies); wings black with white patches; throat white; breast and belly pale buff, flanks washed orange.
  • BillBlack and stout, with a clear hook and tooth at the tip of the upper mandible, used to sever a victim's neck.
  • TailVery long — nearly half the total length — and frequently swung side to side or in circles, a useful mark when perched.

Behaviour

A classic sit-and-wait hunter: perches on a high dead twig, wire or reed tip, drops fast onto prey and returns to the same place to eat it. Strongly territorial when breeding, chasing birds much larger than itself. Caches food by impaling prey on thorns or barbed wire. Lives in open scrub and farmland and is the commonest shrike at low altitude.

Voice

Field recording

0:00 / 0:16
Recording Sharadapte · Licence CC BY-SA 4.0 · Original file

Harsh and grating, like a rusty hinge: 'zha-zha-zha' or 'ge-ge', dry in tone. It also mimics other birds — sometimes better than the original — which is how it draws small birds close enough to catch.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen paddy bunds
  • Jinwan wasteland
  • Qi'ao Island reedbeds
  • scrub at park edges
Field note
A long-tailed bird with a black mask on a paddy-bund wire or a dead twig is almost certainly this species. If you find insects or small lizards hanging on thorns, you have found its larder.
